$ edit b/corpus_test.go  # ./b is a package with tests
$ edit c/corpus_test.go  # ./c is a package with tests
$ edit testdata/top1/base.txtar  # the topology's base, where a package starts
$ edit testdata/top0/base.txtar  # the topology's base, where a package starts
$ go test  # topology-BN-baa-s21-c1-a
    the lift l2 is used by ./c on the path testdata/top0/ → l1 → l2, and ., which owns it, doesn't run it over testdata/top0/, so no package writes its cells of that corpus's cases, which ./c's cells past it are built through.
        A package that uses a lift reaches it from each corpus by the path the lift's owner does: either . runs l2 over testdata/top0/ by that path, or ./c doesn't reach l2 from testdata/top0/. Making a way true may need other registrations to change, such as a lift that would then close a cycle or give a type a second path. If one holds already, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
    what ran, in order:
        l2 ran on base
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/top1
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/top1/base
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/top1/base/l2
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/top1/base/list
FAIL
[exit 1]
$ edit testdata/top0/base.txtar  # delete ./c's cells of top0's base, which no package writes now
$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./c  # topology-BN-baa-s21-c2-c
